blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A colleague adds a year's unspent money as `u = model.add_variable(name="unspent_2029")`, and a reward for unspent money to the objective, which is maximized. HiGHS ends with UNBOUNDED. What is wrong with `u`?

options.text: It is continuous, so HiGHS cannot finish a model that mixes it with binaries
options.says: HiGHS solves models with continuous and integer variables; the selection LP and MILP both ran. The trouble is the bounds.

options.text: It is integer by default, so the reward comes only in whole units
options.says: add_variable makes a continuous variable by default; and whole units would not stop the reward from growing.

options.text: It has default bounds of minus and plus infinity, so it may take any value
options.says: Right: add_variable without lb and ub gives -inf and +inf, so the reward can grow forever. Pass lb=0 and an upper bound, as the formulation's domain says.

options.text: It has default bounds of 0 and 0, so the reward on it is not earned
options.says: The default bounds are -inf and +inf, not 0; a variable stuck at zero could not make the model unbounded.

origin.section: A Variable Is Its Bounds and an Integer Flag, and Its Default Bounds Are Infinite

questions.stem: A rule says a district's crews on call must number between 6 and 14, and `total` is the sum of its crew variables. Which call stores the rule as MathOpt intends?

options.text: `add_linear_constraint(6 <= total <= 14)`, one row with bounds 6 and 14
options.says: Python reads a chained comparison as two comparisons joined by `and`, and MathOpt raises a TypeError rather than drop one half.

options.text: `add_linear_constraint(total <= 14)`, one row with bounds 6 and 14 by default
options.says: A one-sided row stores an infinite lower bound; nothing supplies the 6.

options.text: `add_linear_constraint(total >= 6)` and `(total <= 14)`, two rows, one bound each
options.says: That works, but it is not needed: a ranged row with both bounds finite is one row.

options.text: `add_linear_constraint((6 <= total) <= 14)`, one row with bounds 6 and 14
options.says: Right: the parentheses make one comparison at a time, and MathOpt stores one row with lower bound 6 and upper bound 14.

origin.section: A Constraint Is One Comparison, Stored as lb ≤ expression ≤ ub

questions.stem: A builder calls `model.maximize(npv)` and, further down, `model.maximize(-overtime_cost)` to make overtime count against a plan. What does the solver optimize?

options.text: Minus overtime cost alone, since the second call replaced the first
options.says: Right: maximize sets the whole objective and its sense, so the NPV term is gone. Build npv - overtime_cost as one expression and set it once.

options.text: NPV minus overtime cost, since the second call added to the first
options.says: maximize does not add; the lesson's second call left only the second expression and its offset.

options.text: NPV alone, since the first call fixed the objective of the model
options.says: A later call changes the objective; the lesson's model kept only its second objective.

options.text: NPV first and overtime cost second, since the calls set a ranking
options.says: Ranked goals need auxiliary objectives (lesson 4.3.2); a second maximize call replaces the first.

origin.section: The Objective Is Set by maximize or minimize, and a Second Call Replaces the First
